title: Eight Phases of EMDR
subtitle: A structured protocol beyond eye movements
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical neuroscience diagram illustrating eight phases of emdr across threat, memory, regulation and treatment systems.
learningObjectives: Explain eight phases of emdr in clinically accurate language.
Distinguish established findings from theoretical or mixed claims in eight phases of emdr.
Identify one limitation or safety implication relevant to eight phases of emdr.

sections.explainSimply: EMDR includes history, preparation, assessment, desensitisation, installation, body scan, closure and reevaluation.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: The phases support formulation, consent, stabilisation, target activation, processing, monitoring and follow-up.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Competent delivery requires training, pacing, documentation and adaptation for dissociation, developmental level and complexity.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of eight phases of emdr as one part of a dynamic safety-and-learning system rather than a single switch.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need eight phases of emdr to connect symptoms with learning, context, risk and treatment choice without reducing the person to a brain scan.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Eye movements without the broader protocol are not equivalent to EMDR therapy.
sections.clinicalPearl: Clinical pearl: use eight phases of emdr to sharpen formulation, not to replace phenomenology or outcome measurement.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses eight phases of emdr to formulate triggers, state shifts, avoidance and functional impact, then monitors whether intervention improves daily life rather than relying on presumed neural change.
sections.limitationsCautions: Eye movements without the broader protocol are not equivalent to EMDR therapy. Evidence classification: established protocol standard.
